summary: Adds financial segments and invoiced amounts to the Phase 1 Layercake membership solution (schema Layercake). Every membership event (Join, Change, Lapse, Readmission, Renewal) and paid member can be filtered by payment method, payer type (Individual or Corporate) and concession type. Each Join, Renewal and Readmission event carries the amount invoiced for it, split into subscription and fee, with one headline GBP value (invoiced_subtotal_gbp), a net value and a status that explains any missing amount. Segment values are held once per contact per Campaign Year in a new silv_member_year_attributes table and copied onto every event, with flags showing values carried forward from an earlier year. Every segment uses the same reserved values: Unknown (0), Unrecognised (-1) and Not applicable (-2). Each event is matched to its own invoice, and no invoice is counted on two events. The employer segment is delivered as findings only. Phase 1 counts and measures do not change. This version makes the twelve changes in Damian Watson's review of 20 October 2026 and applies Mike's answers of 23 October 2026. Items that need Finance or real-data profiling stay as open questions, each with a stated working default.

glossary.Campaign Year: The RICS subscription year, as held in Layercake.ref_campaign_year_config and on the invoice source (Subs.tblSubsInvoices.Campaign_Year).
glossary.Eligible invoice: A subscription invoice that may set a contact-year's segments and be matched to an event (RULE-014). Credit notes and enrolment- or application-fee-only invoices are never eligible. A fully credited invoice is eligible only when the contact-year has no other eligible invoice.
glossary.Segment invoice: The eligible invoice that sets a contact-year's payment method, payer type and concession (RULE-079).
glossary.Amount Campaign Year: The Campaign Year whose invoice an event's amounts come from: the event's own year for Renewal and Readmission, and the first paid position's year for a Join (RULE-032).
glossary.Live corporate subscription: A row in Subs.vwCorpSubscriptions for the contact and Campaign Year where both 'Sub Status' and 'Sub User Status' are active (RULE-082).
glossary.Carried forward: A segment value copied from the latest earlier Campaign Year with an eligible invoice, because the year itself has none. Flagged by the *_carried columns.
glossary.Reserved values: Fixed ids in every segment reference table: 0 Unknown (the source has no value), -1 Unrecognised (the source has a value the mapping does not know), -2 Not applicable (no value is expected).
glossary.Headline value: invoiced_subtotal_gbp: the invoiced subscription plus counted fees in GBP, before tax and before credits.
glossary.Invoice source coverage: Campaign Year 2022 onward. Subs.usp_Refresh_SubsInvoices keeps only Campaign_Year >= 2022.

requirements.title: Member-year attributes with payment method
requirements.description: Create Layercake.silv_member_year_attributes, built before silv_membership_events. It holds one row per contact per Campaign Year, from the contact's first membership event to the current Campaign Year. This requirement defines which invoices are eligible: credit notes are excluded, and the case where every invoice is fully credited is defined (review change 5). It also defines which eligible invoice sets a contact-year's segments, and adds payment_method_id and payment_method_carried. REQ-006 and REQ-011 add payer type and concession on the same rules, so all segments use the same invoices (review change 8).

business_rules.rule: The table holds exactly one row per contact per Campaign Year, from the Campaign Year of the contact's first membership event to the current Campaign Year inclusive.

An invoice in Layercake.brnz_subs_invoice for the contact (account_num = contact_no) and Campaign Year is eligible when: (a) it is not a credit note, meaning its invoice number does not contain 'FTCN' and does not contain 'CRE' with a non-zero full_invoice_amount_cur (the owner's own test in Subs.usp_Refresh_SubsInvoices); (b) it is not fully credited (fully_credited is not 'Y'); and (c) its mapped lines are not all enrolment or application fee lines. Where a contact-year has no invoice meeting (a) to (c), its fully credited invoices that meet (a) and (c) are eligible instead (assumes Q-012). A credit note is never eligible.

Where a contact-year has more than one eligible invoice, the latest by trans_date is the segment invoice and sets the year's payment method, payer type and concession (assumes Q-012). Each event's amounts still come from its own invoice (RULE-032).
A contact-year's payment method is the payment mode of its segment invoice (brnz_subs_invoice.inv_payment_method), mapped through silv_ref_payment_method (assumes Q-001).
Where the segment invoice has no payment mode but its payment lines do, the method is the one covering the largest settled amount. On a tie, the method of the earliest payment wins.
A Campaign Year that has an eligible invoice but no payment mode on the segment invoice or its payment lines gets Unknown (0) with payment_method_carried = 0.

A Campaign Year from 2022 onward with no eligible invoice takes the payment method of the latest earlier Campaign Year that has one, with payment_method_carried = 1. If no earlier year has one, it gets Unknown (0) with payment_method_carried = 0 (assumes Q-006).
Contact-years before 2022, the first Campaign Year the invoice source holds, get Not applicable (-2) for payment method, payer type and concession type, with every carried flag 0 (assumes Q-011).

business_rules.rule: silv_ref_payer_type holds the reserved rows 0 Unknown, -1 Unrecognised and -2 Not applicable, plus Individual and Corporate.

A contact is in a live corporate subscription for a Campaign Year when Subs.vwCorpSubscriptions has a row for the contact ('Contact No') with 'Sub Campaign Year' equal to that Campaign Year, and both 'Sub Status' and 'Sub User Status' on that row are active (assumes Q-027 for the active value). A contact-year from 2022 onward is Corporate where its segment invoice (RULE-079) has payment method Corporate and the contact is in a live corporate subscription for that Campaign Year. It is Individual where the contact has a Phase 1 paid position that Campaign Year and the Corporate test fails. Otherwise it is Unknown (0) (assumes Q-002). Years before 2022 follow RULE-080.

Payer type uses the same eligible invoices (RULE-014) and the same segment invoice (RULE-079) as payment method. An enrolment- or application-fee-only invoice sets neither, so payment method and payer type cannot disagree because of it.

A Campaign Year from 2022 onward with no eligible invoice carries forward the payer type of the latest earlier Campaign Year that has one, with payer_type_carried = 1. If no earlier year has one, the payer type is Unknown (0) with payer_type_carried = 0 (assumes Q-006).
corporate_account_ref holds the scheme number ('Scheme No') of the live corporate subscription for Corporate contact-years, and is null for every other contact-year (assumes Q-019).

Every event takes payer_type_id from the attributes row for its contact and segment Campaign Year (RULE-017), or 0 where there is none. fact_membership_events carries it. dim_payer_type is copied from silv_ref_payer_type.

An anomaly row of type CORPORATE_FLAG_NO_SCHEME is written to silv_data_anomaly for each contact-year from 2022 onward whose segment invoice has payment method Corporate but where the contact is not in a live corporate subscription that year (assumes Q-002).

Where a contact-year's segment invoice is settled both by Corporate and by another payment method, one anomaly row of type DOUBLE_PAYMENT is written. requirements.title: Invoiced amounts on Join, Readmission and Renewal events
requirements.description: Each Join, Readmission and Renewal event carries the amount invoiced for it, split into membership subscription and associated fee, so subscription revenue can be reported by segment from the same events that drive membership counts. Each event is matched to its own invoice, and no invoice is counted on two events (review change 2; Mike, 2026-10-23). The event carries subs_amount, fee_amount, invoiced_subtotal, credited_amount and currency_id in invoice currency, and the same amounts in GBP. invoiced_subtotal_gbp is the headline value, net_amount_gbp is invoiced minus credited, and credits are positive (review change 3). amount_status explains every amount, including a missing one (review change 6). Change and Lapse events carry no amounts. fact_membership_events carries the same columns as additive measures.

business_rules.rule: Each Join, Renewal and Readmission event is matched to its own eligible invoice (RULE-014) for its contact in its amount Campaign Year. For Renewal and Readmission that is the event's own Campaign Year. For a Join it is the Campaign Year of the contact's first paid position, or the Join's own Campaign Year where the contact has no paid position (assumes Q-029). Each such event has exactly one invoice (Mike, 2026-10-23).

Within one contact and amount Campaign Year, the events are ordered by event date and the eligible invoices by trans_date, then paired in that order: the earliest event takes the earliest invoice, the next event the next invoice, and so on (assumes Q-022).

Where a contact and amount Campaign Year has more events than eligible invoices, the invoices go to events in priority order: Readmission, then Renewal, then Join, then the earliest event date. Among the events that receive one, invoices are paired by date (RULE-084). Every other event gets no invoice. This fallback only stops an invoice being counted twice.

Where a contact and amount Campaign Year has more eligible invoices than events, the events are paired by date with the latest invoices by trans_date. The earlier surplus invoices are not carried on any event (assumes Q-022).
No eligible invoice's amounts are carried on more than one event.
subs_amount is the sum of the matched invoice's subscription and concession lines, before tax and before credits (assumes Q-021).

On Readmission events, fee_amount is the sum of the matched invoice's readmission fee lines. Enrolment and application fees are not counted on Joins, and no fee type applies to Renewals. fee_amount is 0.00 where no counted fee line exists (assumes Q-003).
invoiced_subtotal = subs_amount + fee_amount.
credited_amount holds the credits raised against the matched invoice as a positive amount, or 0.00 where there are none. Credits never reduce subs_amount, fee_amount or invoiced_subtotal.

Amounts are held in invoice currency with currency_id. The GBP equivalents (subs_amount_gbp, fee_amount_gbp, invoiced_subtotal_gbp, credited_amount_gbp) come from the source's own GBP (accounting currency) amounts. This solution performs no conversion (assumes Q-004).
invoiced_subtotal_gbp is the headline value of an event. net_amount_gbp = invoiced_subtotal_gbp - credited_amount_gbp.
For corporate-funded members, the individual's allocated invoice lines are carried. Firm-level discounts are not spread to individuals and are recorded as a known gap (assumes Q-005).
Change and Lapse events have null subs_amount, fee_amount, invoiced_subtotal, credited_amount, currency_id, every GBP amount, net_amount_gbp and amount_status.
An event matched to a Full Concession invoice carries invoiced_subtotal 0.00, not null.
A Join, Renewal or Readmission event with no matched invoice has null amounts and null currency_id. Its amount_status says why.

Every Join, Renewal and Readmission event has an amount_status, taken from the first case that applies. 'Before invoice data': the amount Campaign Year is before 2022 (assumes Q-011). 'No invoice': no invoice was matched. 'Unmapped lines': the matched invoice has at least one line with line type 'unmapped'. 'Full Concession': the matched invoice's payment_status is 'Full Concession'. 'Fully credited': the matched invoice is fully credited (assumes Q-012). Otherwise 'Invoiced'.

Each of these situations gets its own reason code (anomaly type). Anomalies are limited to the Campaign Years the invoice source covers (review change 11). Anomaly type names are proposals and the design confirms them.

business_rules.rule: The anomaly types in this requirement are raised only for amount Campaign Years the invoice source covers (2022 onward). Events and invoices from earlier years raise none.
Each Join, Renewal or Readmission event whose contact and amount Campaign Year has no eligible invoice gets one anomaly row of type EVENT_NO_INVOICE.
Each eligible invoice in a contact-year where no Join, Renewal or Readmission event takes its amounts from that year gets one anomaly row of type INVOICE_NO_EVENT.
Each event left without an invoice under RULE-085 (more events than eligible invoices) gets one anomaly row of type INVOICE_MATCHES_MULTIPLE_EVENTS, and no EVENT_NO_INVOICE row.
Each surplus invoice under RULE-086 (more eligible invoices than events) gets one anomaly row of type EVENT_MATCHES_MULTIPLE_INVOICES, and no INVOICE_NO_EVENT row (assumes Q-022).

Each Readmission event whose fee_amount is null or 0.00 has exactly one anomaly row explaining why: EVENT_NO_INVOICE or INVOICE_MATCHES_MULTIPLE_EVENTS where it has no invoice, READMISSION_FREE where its invoice has no readmission fee line and the readmission falls under the free-readmission policy (RULE-092), otherwise READMISSION_NO_FEE.
A readmission falls under the free-readmission policy when its event date is between 1 April and 30 June of the calendar year, inclusive (assumes Q-023).

requirements.title: Count-only profiling and coverage queries
requirements.description: Prepare queries that return counts, sums and rates only. Mike runs them on real data and brings the results back as answers, and the agents' tests run them on synthetic data. They cover: the CUSTTRANS_RICS grain profile (Q-021, review change 1); corporate subscription status values (Q-027); payment method coverage; invoiced subtotal coverage and amount_status counts; the Direct Debit share of Partially Paid positions; and totals by payment method, payer type, concession and currency for the last full Campaign Year. In this release there is no pass threshold for real-data results (assumes Q-026).

business_rules.rule: Every query returns aggregates only (counts, sums, rates), never contact-level rows or contact identifiers.

The grain profile groups synapse_fo.CUSTTRANS_RICS invoice rows (TRANSTYPE not 8 or 24, invoice number not containing 'CRE' or 'FTCN') by ACCOUNTNUM and INVOICE. It returns the number of invoices by rows per invoice, by distinct productcode per invoice, and by whether the invoice has a row whose PostingType_Description contains 'tax'. It also returns row counts by RICINVOICETYPE and PostingType_Description, the number of invoices whose summed AMOUNTCUR equals their CustTrans_AmountCur, and the number of Subs.tblSubsInvoices invoices by rows per (Account_Num, Invoice).
The corporate status profile returns row counts of Subs.vwCorpSubscriptions by 'Sub Status' and 'Sub User Status' value.

Payment method coverage is the share of paid positions whose payment method is one of the five methods (payment_method_id above 0), by Campaign Year from 2021. It is also reported by event type, so Change and Lapse events are checked on their own.
Invoiced subtotal coverage is the share of Join, Renewal and Readmission events with a non-null invoiced_subtotal, by Campaign Year, with event counts by amount_status.
Direct Debit share is the share of Partially Paid positions in the current Campaign Year whose payment method is Direct Debit.

For the last full Campaign Year the queries return: paid members by payment method; the corporate count and the corporate share of paid members; the total of invoiced_subtotal_gbp, and the total subscription invoiced (subs_amount) by currency; and paid members by concession type.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Synthetic 2025 data has 8 paid positions: 6 with one of the five methods, 1 Unknown and 1 Unrecognised. Payment method coverage for 2025 is 75.0%, and the same query by event type returns separate rows for Change and Lapse.

Synthetic 2025 data has 10 Join, Renewal and Readmission events, 9 with an invoiced subtotal and 1 with amount_status 'No invoice'. Coverage for 2025 is 90.0%, and the amount_status counts are 9 across the other statuses and 1 for 'No invoice'.

Synthetic last-full-year data has 100 paid members, 16 of them Corporate. The query returns a corporate count of 16 and a corporate share of 16.0%.

No query output contains contact_no or any other contact-level column.

requirements.title: Migrations, rollback and rerunnable loads
requirements.description: Every change ships through the framework migrations (src/sql/deploy/, journal etl.MigrationHistory) with a tested rollback. This is how BR-001's 'migration recorded in schema_migration' is met. Loads are rerunnable.

business_rules.rule: Every new or changed object is deployed by a framework migration with a partner down script. Changes to existing Layercake tables use change scripts that the down script reverses exactly.
Running the full load twice on unchanged source data changes nothing on the second run.
No external object (Subs, synapse_fo, synapse_ce, CE schemas) is created, altered or written to.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: migrations.py check passes, and migrations.py roundtrip passes for every migration in the change.

A second full load on unchanged synthetic data records 0 rows inserted, 0 updated and 0 deleted for every new or changed table in Layercake.etl_run_log, and the silv_data_anomaly row count is unchanged.
migrations.py check reports no change to any external object.

assumptions: Payment method comes from the invoice's payment mode (Subs.tblSubsInvoices.Inv_Payment_Method), with payment lines from synapse_fo.CUSTTRANS_RICS as the fallback. The invoice account number equals the contact number, and the invoice's Campaign Year is used directly (Q-001).

A contact-year is Corporate when its segment invoice has payment method Corporate and the contact is in a live corporate subscription for that year. On a double payment the contact-year is Corporate where a live corporate subscription exists, otherwise Individual (Q-002).

A contact is in a live corporate subscription for a Campaign Year when they exist in Subs.vwCorpSubscriptions for that Sub Campaign Year and both 'Sub Status' and 'Sub User Status' are active. 'Round' is not used, because a round is a tranche of processing corporate records and later rounds may change it (Mike, 2026-10-23). The active value is taken to be 'Active' (Q-027).
Enrolment and application fees are not counted on Joins, and Renewals carry no fee. Only readmission fees are counted, on Readmission events (Q-003).
GBP amounts are the source's own accounting-currency amounts (AMOUNTMST and Inv_Credit_Amount_GBP), with no conversion by this solution (Q-004).
Corporate firm-level discounts are not spread to individuals. The individual's allocated invoice lines are carried, and the discount is a stated known gap (Q-005).
Payment method and payer type carry forward from the latest earlier invoiced year to years with no invoice. Concessions carry forward only when perpetual. Every carried value is flagged (Q-006).
Segment keys are added to the event fact only. Daily detail and the annual rate base keep their grain (Q-007).
The concession reference is CE.vwConcessionType (Q-008).
Practising / Retired status logic is unchanged, and the retirement date keeps driving it (Q-009).
Employer findings use the top 25 employers by paid members in the last full Campaign Year, and count individually funded members with a contact-record employer separately (Q-010).

Campaign Years before 2022, which the invoice source does not hold, get Not applicable (-2) for payment method, payer type and concession, and amount_status 'Before invoice data'. They raise no invoice anomalies (Q-011).

When a contact-year has more than one eligible invoice, the latest by trans_date sets the contact-year's payment method, payer type and concession. When every invoice in a contact-year is fully credited, those invoices stand in as eligible, so events show the invoiced and credited amounts with amount_status 'Fully credited' (Q-012).

Invoices are raised only when a member joins, renews or readmits, so each Join, Renewal or Readmission event has exactly one invoice. A contact with two such events in one Campaign Year has two legitimate invoices (Mike, 2026-10-23). Events and invoices are paired in date order, and where invoices outnumber events the latest invoices are used (Q-022).
There is no Mixed payment method (Q-015).
The standard rate for the concession cross-check is the gross subscription line on the same invoice before the concession (Q-017).
Retired concessions are the six retired item codes used by Subs.usp_Refresh_SubsInvoices, and the comparison covers paid positions (Q-018).
corporate_account_ref holds the live corporate subscription's Scheme No (Q-019).
synapse_fo.CUSTTRANS_RICS holds one row per invoice line with an item code (productcode), and tax appears as its own line, as Subs.usp_Refresh_SubsInvoices treats it (Q-021).
A free readmission is a Readmission whose event date falls between 1 April and 30 June of the calendar year (Q-023).
Removing silv_payment_events.payment_source breaks nothing downstream (Q-024).
Acceptance in this release is on synthetic data only, with no pass threshold for real data (for example minimum payment method coverage) (Q-026).

The Layercake column names used in this spec (for example silv_membership_events.event_date, contact_no, campaign_year and event_type; silv_data_anomaly columns; the Phase 1 paid position) are taken from the v1 draft and the Phase 1 baseline (Q-028).
A Join whose contact has no paid position in any year takes its segments, and looks for its invoice, in the Join's own Campaign Year (Q-029).
out_of_scope: Power BI work: semantic model, DAX and report pages.
Payment method, payer type and concession keys on fact_daily_member_count_detail, fact_annual_rate_base, silv_daily_count_detail and silv_annual_rate_base (working default for Q-007).
Building the employer segment (landing, grouping, key and dimension). This release delivers findings only; full employer segmentation is planned for early 2027 (Q-020).
Spreading corporate firm-level discounts across individuals (working default for Q-005).
Any change to the Practising / Retired status logic (BR-001 Story 4 D5).
apuk_dualmembership: plays no part in this release (Q-025).

Real-data steps, which are done by a human: profiling, reconciliation to Finance figures and spreadsheets, Finance and Corporate team reviews, and traces of real contacts. The agents provide count-only queries.
Editing the Platform Schema document itself. The handover pack supplies its content and a human updates it.
Any change to objects other systems own (Subs, synapse_fo, synapse_ce, CE and other external schemas).

open_questions.question: Is the F&O invoice payment mode (Subs.tblSubsInvoices.Inv_Payment_Method / synapse_fo.CUSTTRANS_RICS.PAYMMODE) the system of record for payment method, and since which Campaign Year is it reliable? Is its grain one value per subscription invoice, with payment lines as the fallback? (RICS Data; BR-001 question 1, Story 1 D1, D2; review section 4)

Is the right test for a corporate-funded member a Corporate payment method on the year's subscription invoice plus a live corporate scheme subscription for that Campaign Year? Or should the scheme code or sub ID alone decide? On a double payment (an invoice settled both by Corporate and another method), should the contact-year be Corporate where a live scheme subscription exists, otherwise Individual? (Finance; BR-001 question 2, Story 2 D1, D3, D5; review 2.3, 2.4 and section 4)

Should an enrolment or application fee count as an associated fee on a Join? Do other fee types exist, for example on Renewals, that should be counted? If Finance counts enrolment fees as membership income, Join values will look low against Finance's figures. (Finance; BR-001 question 3, Story 3 D3; review 1.8)

Should amounts be reported in invoice currency, GBP or both, and which exchange rate applies: the rate posted on the invoice (the source's accounting-currency amounts) or another source? (Finance; BR-001 question 4, Story 3 D4; review section 4)

Should corporate firm discounts (GBP 2,500 or GBP 5,000 for the largest firms) be spread across individuals, or reported at firm level only, with the individual's allocated line carried on the event? How large is the resulting difference from Finance's corporate revenue? (Finance; BR-001 question 5, Story 3 D5; review 1.9)

Where an event's Campaign Year has no invoice (a Lapse, say), should payment method and payer type carry forward from the latest earlier year, flagged as carried forward, or be Unknown? For concessions, the review proposes carrying forward perpetual concessions only, or none. Which? (Finance, Membership Growth; BR-001 question 6, Story 1 D3; review 2.5 and section 4)

Are paid members by payment method, payer type or concession needed day by day? That would change the grain of fact_daily_member_count_detail and fact_annual_rate_base and need a deliberate rebuild. Or are the event and annual views enough? (Finance, Membership Growth; BR-001 question 7)

Which source table is the concession reference (working default CE.vwConcessionType)? Does its key match the concession value on the invoice, and is it complete and current? (Finance, Membership; BR-001 question 8, Story 4 D1)
Should the retired concession or the retirement date drive Practising / Retired status? (Finance, Membership Growth; BR-001 question 9)

How many employers should the employer view cover (proposed: the top 25 by paid members in the last full Campaign Year)? Should it include individually funded members whose contact record names an employer? (Commercial, Corporate team; BR-001 question 10, Story 5 D2, D3)

The invoice source (Subs.tblSubsInvoices) holds Campaign Year 2022 onward only, while Story 1 D4 profiles coverage from 2021. For Campaign Year 2021 and earlier, should segments be Not applicable with amount_status 'Before invoice data', stated as a known limitation (review 2.8, 2.9)? Or should they be derived from an older source, for example synapse_fo.CUSTTRANS_RICS directly?

When a contact has more than one eligible subscription invoice in one Campaign Year, which invoice sets the year's payment method, payer type and concession? Working default: the latest by trans date. Beyond a second event in the year, can more than one live invoice per year be legitimate (for example a mid-year grade change, or a Round 2 individual invoice after a corporate credit)? When every invoice in the year is fully credited, should the fully credited invoice still be used, so the event shows invoiced and credited amounts with net zero and status 'Fully credited', or should the year be treated as having no invoice? (Finance; review 1.5 and section 4)
For a Join, should the segment keys come from the first paid position's Campaign Year (the year its amounts come from) or from the Join event's own Campaign Year?
open_questions.answer: From the same Campaign Year as the Join's amounts, the first paid position's year (Damian Watson, review 1 change 4, 2026-10-20).

open_questions.question: If profiling finds payment mode codes other than Bank, Card, Cheque, DD and Corporate (or an empty string), should they map to Not recorded, get their own entry, or be grouped as Other?
open_questions.answer: They map to a reserved Unrecognised value, kept separate from Unknown (missing) and Not applicable, with the same ids and labels in every segment (Damian Watson, review 1 changes 12 and 2.6, 2026-10-20).

open_questions.question: Should a Mixed payment method value be added, and if so, what share of mixed payers in profiling counts as 'common' (BR-001 Story 1 D3)? Recommendation: decide from the count-only profiling results.
Until a new invoice item code is mapped to a line type, should its amount be left out of subs_amount and fee_amount, or counted under an 'other' amount?
open_questions.answer: Left out until mapped, with the event flagged by an amount status ('Unmapped lines') so the lower figure is explained (Damian Watson, review 1 change 6, 2026-10-20).

open_questions.question: For the Story 4 T5 check that concession members' invoiced subtotal is below the standard rate, what is the standard rate: the gross subscription line on the same invoice before the concession, or a published rate by grade and country (and from which source)?

For the comparison of retired concession and retirement date: which concession types count as retired (the six retired item codes used in Subs.usp_Refresh_SubsInvoices, or the 'Retired Concessions' group in CE.vwConcessionGroup), and which population is compared (paid positions or all members)?

Does the corporate sub ID / scheme number reliably link to the firm, so that corporate_account_ref should be landed (BR-001 Story 2 D4)? Which field holds it: Subs.vwCorpSubscriptions 'Scheme No' or the quote's scheme number?
Should the employer segment be built, or reported as findings only (BR-001 Story 5 D6)?
open_questions.answer: Findings only in this release, as review 1 section 5 recommends (Mike, docs/answers.md, SPEC-001 review 1).

open_questions.question: What is the grain of synapse_fo.CUSTTRANS_RICS: one row per invoice line with an item code, or one row per transaction (one total per invoice, as the Platform Schema describes synapse_fo.custtrans)? Please run the count-only profile in REQ-014 (RULE-095) and bring back the counts. Core query: WITH inv AS (SELECT ACCOUNTNUM, INVOICE, COUNT(*) AS row_cnt, COUNT(DISTINCT productcode) AS item_codes, MAX(CASE WHEN PostingType_Description LIKE '%tax%' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS has_tax_row, CASE WHEN SUM(AMOUNTCUR) = MAX(CustTrans_AmountCur) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS lines_sum_to_total FROM synapse_fo.CUSTTRANS_RICS WHERE TRANSTYPE NOT IN (8, 24) AND INVOICE NOT LIKE '%CRE%' AND INVOICE NOT LIKE '%FTCN%' GROUP BY ACCOUNTNUM, INVOICE) SELECT row_cnt, item_codes, has_tax_row, lines_sum_to_total, COUNT(*) AS invoices FROM inv GROUP BY row_cnt, item_codes, has_tax_row, lines_sum_to_total ORDER BY invoices DESC; plus SELECT RICINVOICETYPE, PostingType_Description, COUNT(*) AS row_count FROM synapse_fo.CUSTTRANS_RICS GROUP BY RICINVOICETYPE, PostingType_Description; plus SELECT rows_per_invoice, COUNT(*) AS invoices FROM (SELECT Account_Num, Invoice, COUNT(*) AS rows_per_invoice FROM Subs.tblSubsInvoices GROUP BY Account_Num, Invoice) x GROUP BY rows_per_invoice. Rules that depend on line grain: RULE-028 to RULE-030 (line-type mapping), RULE-033 and RULE-034 (subscription and fee split, tax excluded), RULE-049 (concession from the invoice's concession line) and RULE-077 (line landing scope). If CUSTTRANS_RICS is transaction grain, those rules cannot be applied from this source. Line-level amounts and the tax split would then need a different source, such as synapse_fo.CUSTINVOICETRANS (invoice lines) and synapse_fo.TAXTRANS (tax), both in the external catalogue. Concessions might instead come from CE.vwConcession (per contact, with apuk_subscriptionyear). That means a new bronze landing and a design change before REQ-007, REQ-008 and REQ-011 are built. (Mike, human profiling step; review 1.1)

When a contact has two or more Join, Renewal or Readmission events taking amounts from one Campaign Year, how is each event matched to its own invoice? The sources hold no direct link between event and invoice. Working default: events ordered by event date are paired with eligible invoices ordered by trans date (earliest with earliest). Where invoices outnumber events, the events take the latest invoices and the earlier surplus invoices are flagged EVENT_MATCHES_MULTIPLE_INVOICES. Is that right, or is there a link (for example ORDERNUM to the CE sales order and quote) that should decide the match?
open_questions.answer: Yes: pair events and invoices in date order; the latest live invoice sets the year's segments.

open_questions.question: Free readmissions in Q2 are policy (review section 3). How is a free readmission recognised in the data? If by date, which Q2: calendar April to June of the event date, the Campaign Year's second quarter, or the RICS fiscal Q2 (the warehouse calendars use July to September, or November to January)? Or is there a flag or item code on the invoice?
Does removing the text column silv_payment_events.payment_source break anything downstream (reports, views or extracts that read it)? (Mike; review section 4)
Should apuk_dualmembership on the concession reference play any part in this release?
open_questions.answer: No. It is unused, per Damian's review, and plays no part in this release (Mike, 2026-10-23).

open_questions.question: Is acceptance for this release on synthetic data only, or should a pass threshold be set for real data, for example a minimum payment method coverage by Campaign Year? (Damian, Mike; review section 4)
open_questions.answer: Synthetic data only, no real-data pass threshold in this release.

open_questions.question: What value do 'Sub Status' and 'Sub User Status' in Subs.vwCorpSubscriptions hold for an active subscription and subscription user? Working default: 'Active'. The count-only status profile in REQ-014 (RULE-096) lists the values.

The dev database could not be queried when this spec was written. Can the Architect confirm the Layercake column names this spec relies on? In particular: the event date on silv_membership_events (taken as event_date), contact_no, campaign_year, event_type, event_nk and event_id; the silv_data_anomaly columns (anomaly_type, contact_no, anomaly_nk, detail); Layercake.etl_run_log; ref_campaign_year_config.campaign_year_end; silv_member_base.retirement_date; and where the Phase 1 paid position is held.

Where a Join's contact has no paid position in any year, should the Join take its segments and look for its invoice in the Join's own Campaign Year (working default), or carry no invoice and Unknown segments?
